anchor: allowing us to make claims about the fundamental bounds on leakage backbone size and quantity.
comment: The evaluated models enforce minimality only under RR, RC and RS (gen_useful_litmus); RI and RO are not checked, so generated tests can carry removable instructions and operands, and the five-relaxation list plus this claim do not describe the tests that were run. It also conflicts with the later Overlapping-interleaving paragraph, which says relaxations are removed.
proposed: Say the shipped models use RR+RC+RS, and that RI/RO are dropped on purpose (the first interleaving round); state which minimality the reported tests satisfy.

anchor: each relaxes to~(d) by the relaxation on its arrow (gray: the part removed), so Alloy does not synthesize them in its initial pass.
comment: The figure's arrows use RO (pane a) and RI (pane b), but those relaxations are not in the evaluated models' minimality predicate, so Alloy does synthesize variants like (a) and (b). Only the RR case (c) is actually filtered.
proposed: Either relabel to the relaxations actually enforced (RR/RC/RS), or say (a)/(b) show the full relaxation set that the first round deliberately relaxes.
evidence: STT_6.als:301-310 (gen_useful_litmus uses RR, RC, RS only); relaxation.tex arrow labels RI/RO/RR

anchor: by iteratively model-finding and blocking discovered graphs until the problem is UNSAT.
comment: No production enumeration reached UNSAT: every campaign is capped by alloy.max_instances (100000 for STT_6), and the OTB shape is missing from the testset precisely because the cap filled first. The same overclaim appears in the intro ('will generate all possible leakage path forms') and the knobs subsection ('coverage is complete up to the instruction bound').
proposed: Say enumeration runs until UNSAT or an instance cap, and report the cap used; soften the 'complete' claims accordingly.

anchor: adds two instructions before which modulate the tracked taint in a way that enables a violation of security guarantees to be seen on a model of STT.
comment: The interleave figure's caption says the shape exposes the ReCon getOldestTaint bug, not an STT violation, and its chain is injected after the committed prefix, not 'before'. Readers also see Fig. ddi-rf captioned as violating STT's predicate, then read here that it 'does not trigger leakage on STT', without being told this means the STT implementation blocks it.
proposed: '...adds a chain of instructions that merges a second speculative source into the ALU op, which exposes the ReCon getOldestTaint bug (Fig. interleave).' Say Fig. ddi-rf is correctly blocked by the STT build.

anchor: Therefore, we define a first round of instruction interleaving, which we do in the Alloy by removing some of the relaxations.
comment: This paragraph motivates an Alloy-side interleaving round with Fig. interleave, but that figure (and its caption) shows the Stage 2 concretization interleaving; the two rounds are conflated. And since dropping RI/RO is what the shipped models do, this 'first round' is the only Alloy round actually used, which contradicts presenting full five-relaxation minimality just above.
proposed: Point the motivation at Stage 2 (Interleaving and State Assignment) or give an Alloy-round example; state plainly that the evaluated models are the relaxed (RR+RC+RS) ones.

anchor: which no single Alloy instance can express; chains off the backbone also add program length and timing variety.
comment: This is wrong per the repo's own analysis: the model can generate the two-source (OTB) shape. Forcing the predicate is SAT, and the shape is absent only because the 100k cap filled with simpler instances first. The interleave caption's 'no Stage 1 instance contains' has the same problem, and its base instance was itself produced with a forcing predicate.
proposed: '...which the capped Stage 1 enumeration did not reach (the model can express it, but the instance cap filled first).'

anchor: Stages~1 and~1.5 use Alloy to enumerate minimal leaking execution graphs from the defense's specification.
comment: The text never mentions a Stage 1.5. Stage 1.5 exists only as an unwired STT prototype that no reported campaign used; every result comes from one flat, capped enumeration. The figure's 'Bounded-exhaustive set' label is also unsupported.
proposed: Either draw the flat pipeline that produced the results, or label Stage 1.5 as the planned two-stage design and map it to the 'first round of interleaving' text; drop 'exhaustive'.
